_comment: The install, in the order you do it. Each group is one download and one instruction, and every row is a path
relative to the folder holding mgs4.exe. tools/install_checks.ps1 reads this; tools/mgs4_dlss.ps1 renders it as
the Setup tab and as --report, and its drag-and-drop uses 'accepts' to know what a dropped file is for.
Versions match the 'setup this was verified on' table in README.md - change both together.
required        a missing file in this group is a failure; files[].optional and files[].required override it
url / urlLabel  where this group's files come from, as a button above them
guide           what to do with them, in the order it is done
accepts         file names this group takes by drag-and-drop; a .zip is unpacked into the game folder
files[].path    relative to the game folder - the row's label

sections.title: 1. The game
sections.blurb: Everything else goes in the folder this sits in.
sections.guide: Metal Gear Solid 4, Master Collection Vol. 2. In its options set Graphics -> API to DirectX 12, FXAA off, vsync off and the frame limiter to 60.

files.detail: one line containing 2492670; lets `mgs4.exe --stage` boot without bouncing through Steam

sections.title: 2. ReShade, with add-on support
sections.blurb: The host this add-on loads into. The plain build looks identical on disk and silently loads nothing.
sections.guide: Download the setup marked "with full add-on support" and run it. Point it at mgs4.exe, pick the Direct3D 10/11/12 renderer, and tick nothing when it offers shader packs - none are needed. It installs itself as dxgi.dll next to the game.

files.detail: ReShade itself, under the name the game loads

sections.title: 3. DLSS and Streamline runtimes
sections.blurb: One zip holds all of these. nvngx_dlss.dll is what DLSS itself needs; the rest are for frame generation.
sections.guide: In the Discord's Pinned Messages, take streamline.zip and extract everything in it straight into the folder with mgs4.exe. It carries the NVIDIA runtimes and the Streamline libraries together, already matched to each other - you do not need the NVIDIA or Streamline SDKs separately. If the NVIDIA app's DLSS override is on for this game it supplies nvngx_dlss.dll instead.

files.detail: DLSS Super Resolution - the one piece DLSS cannot run without
the Streamline entry point the add-on loads

sections.title: 4. DLSS 5 Neural Rendering add-on
sections.blurb: Optional. With this present the add-on runs DLAA on the final image, so NR works at full strength.
sections.guide: From the same Pinned Messages, take the newest renodx-dlss5.addon64 and drop it next to mgs4.exe. Nothing to configure: this add-on notices it and moves the DLAA pass to the composite on its own.

sections.title: 5. This add-on
sections.blurb: Last, so it loads with everything else already in place.
sections.guide: Drop mgs4_dlss.addon64 next to mgs4.exe. The ini beside it is the configuration this was verified with; without it the add-on falls back to its built-in defaults. Building from source instead: dlss-addon\build.bat, then sh dlss-addon/install.sh.

files.detail: its settings; the first run writes the detected InternalRes into it

sections.title: Optional: frame limiter
sections.blurb: The port is built around 60 fps; this is what holds it there.
sections.guide: Needs an ASI loader: winmm.dll next to mgs4.exe (the game imports winmm at startup, so that is what loads the scripts folder), then the .asi and its ini in scripts\ with TargetFrameRate = 60.

files.detail: Ultimate ASI Loader, which loads everything in scripts\

sections.title: Optional: D3D12 fallback
sections.blurb: Only for a build whose Options -> Graphics has no DirectX 12 entry.
sections.guide: Skip this unless the game cannot be asked for DirectX 12 in its own options. The ASI forces the D3D12 backend; where the in-game option exists, leave scripts\MGS4_D3D12.ini at Enabled = 0.

files.detail: forces the D3D12 backend when the game cannot be asked for it
